name: Shakti side test (10 min per side): hippocampal signal
summary: Murphy's side test before any one-sided series: 10 min of the hippocampal signal over the left temporal lobe, where he says it is usually unpleasant, then at once 10 min at the mirror site on the right. It checks for what Murphy calls a 'reversed' structure. The vendor's file is not published; the signal is rebuilt from published descriptions.
setting: Quiet, dim room, eyes closed, relaxed. One coil above each ear: T7 (left) for phase 1 and T8 (right) for phase 2; the other six stay unused. Note how each half feels: pleasant, unpleasant or nothing.
schedule: One signal per test and at most one test every 72 hours (vendor rule).
notes: The vendor: 'To test a signal, apply it over the side that's usually UNPLEASANT for that signal', for ten minutes, 'followed immediately by the same signal over the same location on the other side of the head'; it also allows 'between 5 and 10 minutes on each side' (testsession.htm). This program plays 10 min on the left (T7), then 10 min on the right (T8), one coil per side; Skip ends a side early. T7/T8 and one coil per side are this project's choices: if a one-sided series will use other sites, test there. The hippocampal stand-in is the primed burst: one pulse, then four pulses 170 ms later, three times in 0.74 s (after Tsang 2004 p.5 [1017]), then 4 s of silence. It is rebuilt from descriptions: the vendor's file is not published. Field strength: the vendor's test pages state none. This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. Murphy reads a response opposite to the usual one as a sign of a 'reversed' or 'left-handed' structure, and says: 'If you get no response at all, you probably do not have one'. His side rule rests on user reports and one Persinger-lab study of 40 people, where fields with this pattern were rated more pleasant over the right hemisphere than over the left. That study was not a one-coil test: 1 uT (10 mG), four solenoids per side, each left-right pair on for 10 s, the field on and off in successive 5-min periods for 15 min (Persinger 1994 pp.1-2 [191-192]). Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). Anxiety during a hippocampal session is Murphy's sign that it has run too long: skip or stop. Headache or pressure with hippocampal signals (vendor: about 2%): lower the intensity by one third. Not for people with epilepsy, seizure history or a psychiatric condition; stop on distress.
